title: asymmetric-1to1-cadence-playpad-samir
content:
Context: quick personal prep for weekly PM <> Eng Lead sync. Want to keep this asymmetric — mostly unblockers + short decisions. Intended to be a 25m focused sync + 5m parking lot. Notes to self: keep it tactical, surface tradeoffs, avoid rehashing triage thread unless there is a new ask.

Meeting goals:
- Surface any high-risk customer signals on Dedicated/Private (SLA/regulatory)
- Decide on canary rollback windows for API Console changes (feature flags/metrics)
- Align on routing fallback policy for burst events and cost tiering
- Confirm next steps for KMS/HSM onboarding for first pilot customer

Proposed agenda (timeboxed):
1) 3m quick updates (wins/blocks) — Leah
2) 8m incidents & customer signals (INFR-3421, support threads) — me (Samir)
3) 8m decisions: console canary windows + rollback triggers — Kai
4) 6m architectural alignment: routing policy + dedicated autoscale fallback — joint
5) 5m action items + parking lot — quick wrap

Quick check metrics to call out (one-liners):
- Host API p50/p95 latency: p50 78ms, p95 260ms (last 24h) — small improvement since optimizer patch
- Dedicated pool saturation: east-us-2 avg 72% peak 88% last Tue — check burst capacity config
- Cost delta after small quantization rollout: ~12% tokens saved, some users report coherence drop in chat-mode

Open items / prompts I want answers on:
- Routing fallback: do we prefer model-variant fallback (lower precision) or region-fallback first? trade: cost vs privacy + cold start risk. Need team preference to write policy.
- Canary rollback: current console rollout uses 10% canary with 45m observation window + automated rollback on error-rate > 1.2x baseline. Is 45m enough for noisy workloads? propose extend to 2h for model/schema changes.
- KMS integration: pilot customer requires HSM-backed key wraps. Engineering estimate last sync suggested 3 sprints. Can we compress to 6 weeks if we prioritize? What do we deprioritize?

Notes to surface during discussion:
- Customer A (enterprise) called out that Dedicated pool evictions during maintenance are not clearly signaled — they want a SLA-aligned notification + short maintenance windows. Ops needs a playbook.
- Console change: new route-level analytics introduce an extra DB scan; showed SLO breach in staging for certain routing queries. Might need index/reshard + temporary caching at API layer.
- Private/on-prem: one prospect asked about an air-gapped installer timeline; legal/ops want clear minimum HW profile documented before next sales call.

Draft decisions I'm comfortable taking if no strong objections:
- Expand console canary window from 45m -> 2h for schema/model mapping changes; keep 45m for pure UI changes.
- Routing fallback default: prefer model-variant fallback within same region first (cheaper, lower latency), then region fallback if capacity-constrained; expose explicit knob for customers to opt for region-only.
- KMS/HSM pilot: commit to 6-week expedited path if Sales gets a signed LOI; otherwise default to 3-sprint roadmap.

Action items (clear, owner, due):
- Samir: Draft short rollback policy doc and example triggers (error-rate delta, latency regression, metric drift) — due 2026-03-05
- Kai: Run quick perf run in staging for console route analytics with index + caching patch; report perf numbers + risk by 2026-03-03
- Leah: Coordinate with Solutions Eng to produce minimum HW profile + install checklist for Private (include network reqs, KMS expectations) — due 2026-03-10
- Eng (oncall): Add visibility hook for planned maintenance to Dedicated UI (short-term: banner + API event) — target spike by 2026-03-08

Parking lot / longer-term items (note for roadmap sync):
- Evaluate autoscaler policies to support bursting across capacity tiers (burst to spot GPUs then cold-start warm pool) — needs perf/econ model
- Explore automated quality monitors tied to training evals for quantization rollouts (early-detection of coherence drop)
- Consider tenant-level routing policies (per-tenant fallback profiles) for enterprise customers

Risks / unknowns to surface if asked:
- Extending canary windows impacts time-to-ship and may slow iteration; need to balance with outage risk for schema changes.
- Model-variant fallback requires keeping multiple variants in cache which increases memory footprint; may increase cost for Dedicated customers if we maintain warm variants.
- HSM timelines depend on procurement/legal for customer pilots — we should align Sales expectations now.

Quick script for the start of the meeting (keep short):
- \"Quick status: three things — one win, one risk, one ask.\" (ask is usually a decision, e.g., canary window)

Post-meeting follow-up template (copy into Slack/email):
- Subject: 1:1 recap — decisions & actions (Samir + Kai)
- Body: short summary of decisions (canary window change, routing fallback default, KMS pilot timeline if LOI), list of owners + due dates, link to lightweight rollback doc (I'll post).

Notes-to-self about tone: prioritize clarity, default to shipping-safety (conservative canary on infra/model changes), be explicit about tradeoffs when asking for timeline compression.

Last-minute checklist before hitting the call:
- Attach INFR-3421 thread + canary metrics to calendar invite
- Pull last 24h dedicated pool metrics screenshot (ops dashboard)
- Confirm Leah is on the call and has the install checklist draft

End of doc.
